findings.evidence: `HasLaw` is defined in `Mathlib/Probability/HasLaw.lean` with an `AEMeasurable` field, while lines 188, 288, and 296 require `Measurable T`; the roadmap asks for the graph-plan/transport-map result using `HasLaw` on arbitrary measurable spaces.
findings.fix: Prove the Dirac pushforward formula from `AEMeasurable T (dirac x)` and use `h.aemeasurable` inside the negative theorem; formulate the iff with the necessary a.e.-measurability condition rather than global measurability.
findings.issue: `not_hasLaw_dirac_of_forall_ne` assumes `Measurable T`, although `HasLaw` requires only `AEMeasurable T (dirac x)`; thus the theorem does not exclude all transport maps. The same unnecessary restriction appears in `hasLaw_dirac_iff` (line 288) and `graphPlan_dirac` (line 188).

summary: The Dirac infeasibility API only covers globally measurable maps, not transport maps as represented by `HasLaw`, so it does not establish the claimed acceptance result on arbitrary measurable spaces.
